name: chart: a scatter, then a regression computed over the same columns
description: The first chart scenario that spans two turns and two artifacts. Every other one asks for a single plot, so nothing measured a session that charts, computes, and charts again -- the shape a real exploratory session takes. The second turn names the title because an assertion must not depend on wording the model invented: with the title established by the request, titleContains selects the regression without guessing, and the scatter is selected by its mark instead. Graded on two artifacts rather than one, so a run that overwrites its first chart fails. The fit is graded by the fitted values it plots, not by the tool that produced them: an earlier draft required run_python and failed a run that used vintent's own linear_regression process, which computes a real least-squares fit and is the better route. `yhat` is the column that process writes, and a chart plotting it is one that fitted something. Deliberately not asserting that the regression references the dataset: a fit computed in the browser legitimately embeds the rows it plots, while the scatter is expected to reference, which is what separates the two.
inputs: Plot Glucose against BMI from the dataset in this history as a scatter plot, using vintent.
Now fit a linear regression between those same two columns and chart the fit as a second plot titled "Linear Regression".
